{{< include assets/webr-knitr.md >}}

This page runs R **inside your browser** (with [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/)). Nothing to install, nothing saved: reload the page and everything starts again. The first visit downloads about 10 MB (R itself) and takes a few seconds; prefer Wi-Fi.

Use it to try the basics before Session 1, or if R is not installed yet on your computer. For the course itself, work in RStudio: that is where your project, data and scripts live.

## 1. R as a calculator

Edit the numbers, then press **Run Code**.

```{webr}
2 + 2
(1 + 0.03)^10      # 3% growth for 10 years
sqrt(16)
```

## 2. Objects

`<-` stores a value under a name. Type the name to see the value.

```{webr}
gdp_pc <- 72829    # United States, 2022, GDP per capita (PPP $)
pop    <- 334      # millions
gdp_pc * pop / 1e6 # total GDP, in billions of PPP $
```

## 3. Vectors and missing values

A vector holds several values of the same type. `NA` marks a missing value.

```{webr}
countries <- c("United States", "China", "India")
life_exp  <- c(77.4, 78.2, 71.7)   # 2022, years
mean(life_exp)

gini <- c(41.8, NA, 23.0)   # US and India 2023; China blanked for the example
mean(gini)                  # NA: one value is missing
mean(gini, na.rm = TRUE)    # ignore the missing value, and say so
```

## 4. A small data frame

A data frame is a table: one row per country, one column per variable.

```{webr}
df <- data.frame(
  country    = c("United States", "China", "India"),
  gdp_pc_ppp = c(72829, 21499, 8347),
  life_exp   = c(77.4, 78.2, 71.7)
)
df
df[df$life_exp > 75, ]
df$gdp_pc_ppp / df$gdp_pc_ppp[3]   # how many times India's level
```

## 5. Your turn

Add a column `richer_than_china` that is `TRUE` when GDP per capita is above China's, then print `df`.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_1
df <- data.frame(
  country    = c("United States", "China", "India"),
  gdp_pc_ppp = c(72829, 21499, 8347)
)
df$richer_than_china <- ______
df
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_1"}
Compare the column with China's value, the second element: `df$gdp_pc_ppp > df$gdp_pc_ppp[2]`.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_1"}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_1
#| solution: true
df$richer_than_china <- df$gdp_pc_ppp > df$gdp_pc_ppp[2]
df
```
:::

<small>Source of the values: World Bank, World Development Indicators (WDI), 2022, as in the course data. Gini: latest year available (2023); the China value (36.0 in 2022) is left out on purpose to show `NA`.</small>
